app/next.config.ts:3-8 — only long-stable config: poweredByHeader, compress, turbopack.root (top-level stable option, confirmed in Next docs)
app/app/layout.tsx:7 — export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic', stable since Next 13.4

reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs; every framework feature used (App Router conventions, generateMetadata, notFound, usePathname/useRouter, server-only) has been stable for over a year, most for two-plus years.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:1-47 — data fetching + caching isolated in one server-only module behind get/find/list
app/lib/data.ts:1-12 — all API-shape knowledge and derived indexes centralized in one module
app/components/Filters.tsx:2 — client-side navigation APIs confined to two small components (Filters, GameSelect)
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain, and even the framework-touching seams (data layer, router usage) are wrapped in a few small modules, so any future swap would be trivial.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:14-47 — hand-rolled in-memory TTL cache with cache:'no-store' fetches satisfies the spec's live-data requirement without reaching for unstable_cache, revalidateTag, or Cache Components
app/app/layout.tsx:7 — force-dynamic is the honest, stable way to meet 'no data embedded at build time'
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all; where the framework offered newer-but-less-settled options (caching model, unstable_cache), the app chose stable equivalents that fully meet the spec.

findings.issue: The app uses the classic caching model (force-dynamic + no-store) rather than the Cache Components model that Next.js 16.4 now recommends and enables by default in create-next-app (it becomes the default in Next 17).
findings.suggestion: No action needed now; when upgrading to Next 17, budget a migration to cacheComponents/'use cache' — the isolated data layer in app/lib/api.ts makes this a contained change.

findings.issue: next is pinned to an exact version (16.4.3) with no range, which is current-stable today but couples the app to a specific patch.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for a judged build; for a long-lived codebase consider a caret range on the 16.4 line.

summary: The app is maximally conservative: not a single experimental, preview, RC or canary API appears anywhere, and the framework version pinned (16.4.3) is the latest stable release. Caching is hand-rolled in one server-only module rather than leaning on unstable_ or flag-gated APIs, which is both spec-compliant and low-risk. The only forward-looking note is that the classic force-dynamic model will face migration pressure when Next 17 makes Cache Components the default, and the contained data layer makes that migration cheap.
